analyst_view.overall: Early view: Viking won their first ever Champions League game 4-1 against Sabah on matchday 4 and have scored in 12 European games in a row, while Feyenoord were beaten 3-0 at home by Inter and have one win from four. Both are around the play-off line (Viking 22nd, Feyenoord 32nd), so with two rounds left after this a defeat would hurt Feyenoord far more. Matchday 5 comes first, so team news is refreshed nearer the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, 2.4 of them Viking's. I stay close to that: Viking's last seven home games before Sabah each had three or more goals and the 4-1 made it eight, while Feyenoord have conceded 11 in four league-phase games. The doubt is Feyenoord's end of it, with four goals all campaign and none against Inter.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners and give Feyenoord the bigger share (6.3). I lean lower: Feyenoord have been second-best away from De Kuip (5-1 at Barcelona, 1-0 at Betis), and Viking, with Christiansen and Tripic driving their attack, should have more of the ball at home than this split suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean a little higher because of the stakes: Feyenoord sit 32nd on three points, so a loss in Stavanger would leave them needing a lot from their last two games, and that kind of pressure usually brings late, desperate fouls. The referee has not been named.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 15.6. I lean lower on Feyenoord's side: Giovanni van Bronckhorst's team managed four goals in four games and were shut out at home by Inter, and Viking at home have dictated games rather than sat back.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. I lean a little lower, mainly because Feyenoord's attack (Hadj Moussa, Ferri, Valente) has rarely tested goalkeepers in this competition. Viking's own share of around six looks fair given how they finished against Sabah.
